text:
nico: Hi team, first-week onboarding question — I'm running a quick customer-facing PoC from my laptop using a hosted API key and seeing intermittent 429s and occasional truncated streams. What's the low-friction way to get a short demo bump vs a sandbox key, and does IT need any specific headers/IPs whitelisted?
onboard-bot: Welcome Nico! :tada: For demo bumps DM dev-support or post here with the demo window and expected QPS. See the new-hire checklist: https://redwood.dev/onboarding
dev-support: Hi @nico  we can approve 24/48/72h hosted bumps (requires demo window + expected QPS) or issue a sandbox key immediately (sandbox has separate quota). Sandbox is fastest if you need same-day access.
netsec: Two things for IT: 1) Allow outbound to api.redwood.ai and our published egress CIDR. 2) Ensure the corporate proxy doesn't terminate/chunk/aggregate streaming responses (some proxies strip `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` or buffer HTTP/2 frames). If they require a header, ask them to allow `X-Forwarded-For` and not to mutate `Authorization` or `Content-Length`.
sam: When you hit 429 paste the response headers (redact the key). Look for `x-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-reset`, `x-request-id`, and `retry-after` if present. If `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0` and a reset time is present it's quota. If you see `Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` it's likely network/proxy. Also include the curl you ran.
nico: paste sanitized curl and headers:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-hosted-REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-1-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' -N -v
```
Response snippet: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
x-request-id: req_f3e2d1
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
(no retry-after)
Also saw `Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` intermittently during streaming attempts.
dev-admin: Quick guidance: if you need demo fidelity identical to hosted, request a hosted bump and include demo window + expected token/embedding units. If you want minimal friction, ask for a sandbox key (issued via DM) — same protocol, separate quota. For repeated demos we recommend setting up ephemeral Vault creds. Hosted bumps require a short approval workflow (growth/billing signoff for customer-facing demos).
netsec: If the proxy NATs many users to one egress IP you can trip IP-level buckets. IT can either whitelist your machine's public IP or add an exception for `api.redwood.ai` to avoid pooling. Also check for HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation on proxies; forcing `--http1.1` in curl can help debug.
sam: Troubleshooting checklist: 1) Try from a phone hotspot (off corporate network) to see if 429s persist. 2) If off-network works, it's proxy/NAT bucket. 3) If off-network still 429s, paste `x-request-id` and we'll trace gateway logs. 4) Add exponential backoff with jitter client-side and batch requests (embeddings/chat) to reduce QPS.
nico: For demo I need 15 minutes of streaming traffic, peak ~8 req/s. I'd prefer sandbox if it's identical.
dev-support: Sandbox it is — will DM a sandbox key valid for 48h. For future customer demos, include expected token/embedding usage and we can route a hosted bump request (takes a bit longer).
ops-bot: Please redact keys in any pasted logs. Do not share secrets in channels.
netsec: Note for IT: you might need to allow `Connection: keep-alive` and avoid aggressive idle timeouts for long streams. If token expiry is suspected, check for 401 vs 429 (401 = auth/TTL, 429 = quota).
sam: If you ever see no `retry-after`, the gateway still enforces a reset window via `x-rate-limit-reset` or internal buckets; `x-request-id` is the fastest way for us to correlate.
nico: Thanks everyone, will test hotspot, accept the sandbox key, and DM dev-support. Appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:
